scope: B2wPiper, OFFICIAL ATEC-TaskB-B2wPiper env, single env, seed 42, cameras ENABLED and recorded. ORACLE probe: the base is parked from the object's true pose, so this measures the delivery mechanics and shows them, not perception or a policy.
claim: The official objects_in_circle reward fires while the run is on camera. This is the same oracle delivery as task_b/results/oracle_delivery.json, re-run with the cameras kept alive so the run could be recorded; it is not a policy result and not a Task B pass.

reproduces_the_camera_free_run_exactly.note: identical step count, identical score to six significant figures and the same two scoring steps, so keeping the cameras on changed nothing the probe consumes -- same oracle plan, same action terms, same physics

source_video.layout: head RGB (640x480) | wrist RGB (640x480), one row
source_video.kept_local: over GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit, so only the re-encode below is committed

transformation: full 1x recording, unchanged frame count and timing, pad 1280x480 to 1280x720; lossy H.264 re-encode only; no generated frames or edited robot motion
ffmpeg_version: ffmpeg version 4.4.2-0ubuntu0.22.04.1 Copyright (c) 2000-2021 the FFmpeg developers

what_to_watch.timeline_source: the probe's own phase record in trace.jsonl, in policy seconds; the recording is 10 fps against a 50 Hz policy, so media time equals policy time exactly
what_to_watch.0.0_s: REACH -- the two-stage reach begins from the settled stance
what_to_watch.2.7_s: CLOSE -- the jaws close on the bottle; the wrist view fills with yellow
what_to_watch.6.2_s: LIFT -- the bottle leaves the ground
what_to_watch.10.2_s: CARRY -- the drive to the bin, bottle held, 30 s long; the wrist view keeps it in frame with its label legible (verified stills at 12.1 s, 38.1 s and 42.1 s)
what_to_watch.40.7_s: PLACE_RAISE -- the bottle comes up over the bin's 0.50 m lip
what_to_watch.43.2_s: PLACE_DRIVE -- the inward move past the wall
what_to_watch.43.9_s: objects_in_circle fires (step 2195). The on-frame raw score flips 1 -> 2.
what_to_watch.46.6_s: RELEASE -- the jaws open and the object drops
what_to_watch.watch_out: The raw score reads 1 from 0.7 s onward. That is the official grasped_objects proximity term firing at spawn -- the gripper body starts within its 0.20 m threshold of an object -- and it is NOT a grasp. The grasp itself is the LIFT at 6.2 s; the second point, at 43.9 s, is the delivery.

caveat: The overlay and the score come from the evaluator. The raw recording is 105 MB and is not in git; the committed file is a re-encode of it, so its hash is a hash of the re-encode.
